master.title: Daily headlines from Japan
master.content:
Two fatally shot during GSDF training exercise

Two men aged 52 and 25 were fatally shot and another wounded on Wednesday at a Ground Self-Defense Force shooting range in the city of Gifu during a live-fire training exercise for SDF candidates, with an 18-year-old man arrested on the spot on suspicion of attempted murder. The incident has rocked the country, as SDF personnel are one of the few professions authorised to carry guns in Japan, where gun crime remains rare. According to media reports, the suspect, who was an SDF candidate soon to complete his three-month education and training period, shot the three GSDF members who were overseeing the exercise with an automatic rifle. The older of the two fatalities was the teacher, and media reports say the suspect had been scolded just before the shooting took place. (Asahi, Yomiuri, Mainichi, Sankei, Tokyo Shimbun, Nikkei)

Trump pleads not guilty to all 37 charges

Most major Japanese dailies reported on their front pages the news that former US President Donald Trump on Tuesday pleaded not guilty to all 37 charges brought against him in connection with the classified government documents found at his Florida estate at his arraignment at a Miami courthouse. Japanese media speculate on what the latest allegations might mean for his attempt to again run for the White House. (Yomiuri, Mainichi, Sankei, Tokyo Shimbun, Nikkei)

European Parliament backs regulations for AI

Several major Japanese dailies reported on their front pages the European Parliament's support for legislation that would regulate artificial intelligence (please see below for the headlines), showing how Japanese media continue to closely follow development in this field. The focus of the articles was that the new rules would oblige companies to disclose if content was generated by AI, and also that consideration of copyrights would also be required. (Yomiuri, Mainichi, Sankei, Nikkei)

Surge in survey respondents who think Japan-South Korea ties 'good'

A sharp upturn in positive sentiment in both Japan and South Korea over their impression of bilateral relations was observed in a recently conducted media poll, reflecting the efforts by the governments of the two countries to improve ties after years of tension. According to the results of a joint poll by the Yomiuri Shimbun of Japan and the Hankook Ilbo of South Korea, 45% of Japanese and 43% of Korean respondents said they thought current Japan-ROK relations were 'good'. This is a huge improvement from a similar surve last year, when the figure stood at 17% on both sides. There was a 10-point increase in the percentage of Japanese who said they could 'trust' Korea to 40%. While only 28% of Koreans said they could trust Japan, up just three points from last year, the figure was still a record high since the question first appeared in this poll in 1996. (Yomiuri)

Toyota board secures shareholders' backing

Toyota Motor Corp. secured shareholder backing for all 10 board directors - including Chairman Akio Toyoda and President Koji Sato - that it had put forward at an annual general meeting on Wednesday, despite advice from US proxy advisory company Glass Lewis to vote against the proposal to reappoint Toyoda on the basis that there were too few board members who could be considered independent. Shareholders also rejected the first investor proposal to be put forward at the automaker's general meeting in 18 years, which called for greater disclosure of the firm's climate lobbying. (Nikkei)

EP adopts bill obliging generative AI to take copyrights into consideration (Yomiuri, 200 words)

EP backs legislation obliging clarification of AI-generated content (Mainichi, 355 words)

EU legislature backs AI regulation (Sankei, 275 words)

EU adopts bill to regulate AI (Nikkei, 295 words)

EU eyes setting AI rules for companies to follow by year's end (Yomiuri, 420 words w/table)

EU says Google's online ads violate antitrust laws (Nikkei, 265 words w/photo)

European Commission urges breakup of Google (Asahi, 250 words)

Google 'violating antitrust laws', European Commission says (Yomiuri, 170 words)

EU: Google violating antitrust laws (Mainichi-Kyodo, 150 words)

Prepared based on the vernacular press by Mari Koseki

Chief Press Officer, Political, Press and Information Section, EU Delegation to Japan
